contents.heading: Common Challenges in Securing Plot-Only loan
contents.secHeading: Getting a plot loan in India is tougher than a home loan due to:

list.heading: Limited Availability & Location Restrictions –
list.desc: Plot loans are harder to get and usually approved only for plots within municipal limits.

list.heading: Higher Costs & Shorter Tenure –
list.desc: Interest rates (8.5%–11%) are higher than home loans, with a shorter repayment period (10-15 years).

list.heading: Strict Eligibility & Legal Issues –
list.desc: Requires high income, strong credit score, and clear land titles to avoid ownership disputes.

list.heading: Mandatory Construction & Fewer Tax Benefits –
list.desc: Many banks impose a construction clause, and tax benefits are limited compared to home loans.

listUrl.linkName: Learn More About Plot Loan Challenges →

contents.listSecPara: 💡 Tip: Before applying, check if your lender allows plot purchase without mandatory construction to avoid future complications.

cards.heading: Residential Plot Loan
cards.para: A loan designed for individuals looking to purchase a plot for building a home in a residential area. Some lenders may require you to start construction within a specific timeframe.

cards.heading: Commercial Plot Loan
cards.para: This type of loan is for buying land intended for commercial use, such as office spaces, retail outlets, or warehouses. Interest rates and eligibility criteria may differ from residential plot loans.

cards.heading: Agricultural Land Loan
cards.para: A loan provided for purchasing farmland, often restricted to individuals engaged in farming or agriculture. Some countries have regulations on who can buy agricultural land.

cards.heading: Investment Plot Loan
cards.para: For those looking to buy land purely for investment purposes without immediate plans to develop it. These loans may have stricter conditions since they don’t involve immediate construction.

contents.heading: Why balance transfer is not allowed for Plot-Only loan?

list.heading: No Balance Transfer for Plot-Only Loans –
list.desc: Plot-only loans are generally not eligible for balance transfer, as lenders prefer financing properties with immediate construction plans. Without a building project, the risk for banks remains high, limiting refinancing options. However, there’s a way to work around this restriction by upgrading your loan type.

list.heading: Balance Transfer Denied? Try Upgrading! –
list.desc: If you have a plot-only loan, transferring it to another lender isn’t usually possible. Lenders prefer loans linked to property development, which ensures a tangible asset backing the loan. The good news? You can still restructure your loan by converting it into a Plot + Construction Loan for better terms.
